output.title: Measure email threading before you automate it
output.body:
If you are thinking about email threading, treat it as a workflow decision first, not a software feature. The real question is simple: are you losing time because replies are hard to follow, context is split across inboxes, or follow-ups drift? If the answer is only occasional annoyance, automation is probably the wrong place to spend attention. A cleaner mailbox habit may be enough.

Start with a manual check: review one week of email activity and mark every thread that went off track. Note what broke the thread, how long it took to recover, and whether the same pattern kept showing up. That gives you a grounded view of whether the problem is real before anyone reaches for tools. No need to turn every inbox wobble into a project; email has enough drama already.

If the issue keeps repeating, the bounded decision is whether to tune your existing email or CRM setup, or whether the workflow is specific enough to justify a small AI-assisted pilot for categorisation or routing. Keep that pilot narrow. Do not mix it with bulk email, compliance-heavy correspondence, or anything that would require autonomous decisions. Human approval stays in place for any high-risk step.
